newsitem.title: USA: US stocks rally, Dow and S&P storm to record close.
newsitem.headline: US stocks rally, Dow and S&P storm to record close.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied sharply on Monday with the Dow Jones industrial index storming into record territory with a gain of more than 120 points amid higher oil prices and a slide in the dollar, which fell to its lowest level against the yen since January on Monday.
The 30-stock Dow index surged 1.7 percent, climbing 123 to 7293, breaking its closing high record for the 18th time so far in 1997.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index also moved to an all-time high close, adding 1.6 percent or 13 to 838.

Multinationals gained on the weaker dollar as expectations rose for higher profits at U.S. companies that do business abroad. General Electric Co added 1-3/4 to 59-7/8 in heavy trading after a stock split. Walt Disney Co, DuPont Co, Merck and Co Inc, and Procter & Gamble all posted sharp gains.
Every Dow component except two, Caterpillar Inc and McDonald's Corp closed higher.
But the rally in blue chips was not matched in smaller stocks, which have posted significant gains recently.
The Nasdaq Composite closed up nine points to 1344, or 0.7 percent and the Russell 2000 added roughly the same amount on a percent basis, rising 2.3 to 363.8.

"We're seeing continuing demand for big-name first-tier stocks. Today was a continuation of the bullish trend, but small cap stocks may not have the follow-through," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist for Prime Charter Ltd.
"One to two percent swings in the Dow are becoming very commonplace these days," he said.

Oil stocks rallied as crude oil prices hit their highest level in two months, after a U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Strait of Hormuz amid new Iranian wargames in the Persian Gulf, home to the majority of the world's oil supply.
Chevron Corp shares hit a new 52-week high, adding 1-5/8 to 72 and Exxon Corp rose 1-1/2 to 59-3/8.
June crude oil closed up 95 cents to $21.38 a barrel in New York after hitting the new two-month $21.55 high earlier.
Some market watchers questioned whether stocks can hold the gains in the face of several key inflation and economic reports this week.

"We could have a problem. If the numbers come in strong, stocks will lose these gains. And if there is evidence of a weakening, people could start to worry about corporate earnings," said Henry Herrmann, president and chief investment officer at Waddell & Reed.
Bonds kept a firm tone ahead of the reports with the long bond up 2/32 to yield 6.89 percent.

Tuesday, retail sales are due ahead of the market opening with economists forecasting a 0.3 pct drop on average. On Wednesday, the government reports on wholesale inflation and on Thursday, April retail inflation numbers are due.
Despite rising oil prices, airline stocks also rallied.

International Business Machines Corp jumped 4-3/8 to 171-7/8, nearing its all-time historical high of 175-7/8. The gains came on the renewed interest in big cap stocks and the weaker dollar, and followed IBM's major publicity coup over the weekend when its Deep Blue supercomputer made chess history by defeating world champion Garry Kasparov.
Semiconductor stocks were one of the only sectors that did not participate in the rally. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Semiconductor Index fell nearly two percent.
Citrix Systems Inc shares rocketed nearly 70 after it won a pact to develop terminal support for Microsoft Corp's Windows NT Server network operating system. Citrix shares rose 13-3/8 to 32-5/8.

Shares of British Grand Metropolitan Plc, the owner of the Burger King, jumped 4-3/4 to 38-7/8 on the NYSE after it said it would merge with beermaker Guinness Plc. Guiness owns the Johnnie Walker brand of scotch.
The S&P 500 rose 12.88 to 837.66, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite gained 9.14 to 1344.19.
Volume on the NYSE was 437.5 million shares.
((-- Wall Street Desk, 212-859-1881))
